content.title: About
content.content: Salmon salad is a dish where the main ingredient is boiled or smoked salmon, cut into cubes or strips, mixed with vegetables (cucumber, tomato, leafy greens), herbs, and a light dressing made from olive oil, lemon juice or yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon is one of the few fish that contains significant amounts of the omega‑3 fatty acids EPA and DHA.
Smoked salmon is a staple of Scandinavian cuisine and is known as “gravlax”.
Salmon salads are often served at festive tables in Japan as sushi‑rolls without rice.
Salmon can be farm‑raised, making it more affordable but influencing its nutrient profile.
Pairing salmon with citrus (lemon, lime) enhances iron absorption from the vegetables.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Salmon provides a complete set of essential amino acids needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The salad supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Salmon contains selenium, potassium and phosphorus, essential for immunity, blood‑pressure regulation and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Unlike many meat products, salmon is predominantly composed of beneficial polyunsaturated fats.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to salmon, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Although salmon generally has low mercury levels, pregnant women and children should limit consumption of large predatory fish.

items.title: Smoked salmon and sodium
items.content: Smoked varieties often contain high salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly stored salmon can harbor salmonella or listeria; maintaining the cold chain is essential.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve salmon salad chilled, often with avocado slices, boiled eggs, olives or nuts. Dressing can be made from olive oil, lemon juice, mustard and fresh herbs. It pairs well with whole‑grain bread or flatbreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. If the salmon is raw or only partially cooked, store it separately at 0‑4 °C.
